sections.html:
Cherokee County deeds are recorded at the Register of Deeds in Murphy, Suite 126-A, 75 Peachtree Street. Call 828-837-2613. Land records are accepted between 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. The same counter also takes survey plats, UCC statements and soldier discharges, certifies notaries, and holds the county's birth, death and marriage records.

About 30,830 people live in the county, in 19,158 housing units, and 83.7% of homes are owner-occupied. The typical owned home was valued at $232,300 for 2020 to 2024, and owners paying a mortgage spend a median of $1,242 a month. That is a settled, moderately priced market, so closing costs like deed stamps are modest next to the equity in most houses.

A deed runs $26 for the first fifteen pages, and a deed of trust is $64 for the first thirty-five. Every page beyond those counts adds $4.

Plats filed since October 1991 must be on mylar transparent plastic, in 18 by 24, 21 by 30 or 24 by 36 inch sizes. These amounts follow the uniform schedule in G.S. 161-10, and recording the cancellation of a deed of trust carries no fee.

Cherokee prices its stamp at $2 per $1,000 of purchase price, which is the same rate the state states as $1.00 per $500. Under G.S. 105-228.30 the person transferring the property owes it, payable to the register before the deed is filed. Half funds the county general fund and half goes to Raleigh.

For a seller, that comes down to a few points:

  • Expect the stamp tax on the seller's side of the settlement statement.
  • Price steps are counted in $500 slices, and any leftover fraction rounds up to the next slice.
  • Under G.S. 47-18, options, contracts to convey and leases longer than three years do not bind later purchasers and lien creditors until they are registered in the county where the land sits.

sections.h2: Looking up tax and deed information
sections.html:
The county's interactive tax viewer displays tax amounts from 2008 forward. It refreshes each morning at 6 a.m., so a payment appears the next day. The data was built for the county's own use from recorded deeds and plats, and the viewer asks users to confirm anything important against the public record.

For questions about a value, a parcel record, or a difference between the viewer and a deed, call the Cherokee County Appraisal Office at 828-835-3296. The register of deeds in Murphy keeps the original recorded deed. A certified copy is $5 for the first page and $2 for each page after.

sections.h2: Tax relief that changes when you sell
sections.html:
Older, disabled and veteran owners request relief locally through the county assessor. For 2026, an owner 65 or older (or disabled) with income of no more than $38,800 can exclude the larger of $25,000 or half the appraised value. The disabled veteran exclusion shields the first $45,000 and has no age or income cap. Apply on form AV-9 by June 1 ahead of the tax year. The rules are in G.S. 105-277.1 and G.S. 105-277.1C.

If you receive one of these benefits now, ask the Appraisal Office what a sale does to it before you sign a contract.

Vital records are handled at the same counter, and a few of them matter during a sale. Heirs often need a death certificate, a marriage license or certificate can affect who signs a deed, and notaries can be booked by appointment.

  • Certified birth, death and marriage certificates: $10 each, with requests directed through the county's vital records portal.
  • Marriage license: $60.
  • Notary appointment: $10 each.
  • Copies of any record: $0.10 apiece.

If heirs need a certified certificate, order it early so the title company has it when the file is reviewed.

Handle the tax bill, the payoff and the title work first, then let the closing attorney file. Bills are due September 1 and begin collecting interest on January 6 under G.S. 105-360. The lien follows the parcel from the listing date, so the closing office usually pays the current bill from the sale proceeds.

A few steps keep things moving.

  • Confirm every owner on the chain of title, heirs included if the house was inherited.
  • If lot lines are unclear, ask a surveyor about plats. A plat is its own $21 filing.
  • Collect payoff letters for any deed of trust. The register records the release for free.
  • Pull your own vesting deed so the legal description in the new deed matches it word for word.

The register of deeds records documents but does not draft them, so hire a North Carolina attorney to prepare the deed. If repairs, liens or disagreeing heirs have stalled the sale, a cash purchase sidesteps a lender's timetable. Our North Carolina page explains that route.

faqs.q: Where is the Cherokee County register's office?
faqs.a: 75 Peachtree Street, Suite 126-A, Murphy, NC 28906. Call 828-837-2613, and bring land records in by 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: What does recording a Cherokee County deed cost?
faqs.a: A deed up to 15 pages is $26, then $4 a page. Deeds of trust are $64 up to 35 pages, and a plat filing is $21.

faqs.q: How are Cherokee County deed stamps figured?
faqs.a: At $2 for each $1,000 of price, the same rate the state writes as $1.00 per $500. The seller pays it when the deed goes on record.

faqs.q: Who answers questions about a Cherokee County tax value?
faqs.a: The Cherokee County Appraisal Office, at 828-835-3296, handles questions about parcel data and values.

faqs.q: Is there a charge for deed copies?
faqs.a: Yes. Plain copies are ten cents a page. A certified document is $5 for page one and $2 per page afterward, and vital record certificates are $10 each.
